governing: steel.bolts: eccentric bolt group by the elastic method (e = a = 2.25 in), the weakest bolt set by tearout of the 1/4 in plate at the bottom bolt (AISC 360-22 J3.7, J3.11a): demand 11.50 kip, capacity 11.88 kip
notes: Petra PASS on try2.petra (= final.petra), 19 of 19 obligations certified, ASD, service shear 0 to 45.988 kip signed task.owner@example.org / task 303-006. Design: conventional single plate, A572 Gr 50 PL 1/4 x 3-3/4 x 1'-3 1/4, five 3/4 in A325-N (Group 120, threads included) snug-tight bolts in standard holes at 3 in pitch, Lev 1-5/8 in, plate Leh 1-1/2 in, beam-web edge 1-3/4 in as detailed (1-1/2 in after the 1/4 in underrun), bolt line a = 2-1/4 in = 1/2 in setback + 1-3/4 in, top bolt 2-7/8 in below the beam top, E70 3/16 in fillet both faces of the plate to the W10x49 web. Other high checks: beam_fit 0.978 (plate edges 1.25 in and 1.2 in from the beam's outer flange faces, clear of kdet 1-1/8 in as well as kdes), shear rupture 0.867, block shear 0.852, base metal 0.619, weld 0.542. The horizontal edge distances on the plate and beam web sit exactly at the Manual's 2d = 1-1/2 in ductility minimum (detailing utilisation 1.0, compliant); do not cut them short. Petra's bolt check is conservative (full a as eccentricity, elastic method). Not checked by Petra: axial tool room between the column flanges is about 4 in from the plate or beam web to each W10x49 flange, too short for an in-line impact wrench, so snug the bolts with a spud wrench or right-angle tool (snug-tight, as drawn); bolt lengths are not checked (grip about 0.55 in). Keep threads included: with plies this thin, threads-excluded could not be assured.
